LESSON: FAMILY NEEDS (EMOTIONAL NEEDS)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social Environment
Topic 1.2: Family Needs (Emotional needs)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Family Needs (Emotional needs), part of Social Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do people express the way they feel?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify different types of emotions expressed by people in daily life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Family Needs (Emotional needs) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use facial expressions to express different types of emotions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Family Needs (Emotional needs) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. describe ways in which emotional needs are met in real life situation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Family Needs (Emotional needs) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. illustrate different emotions expressed by self and others,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Family Needs (Emotional needs) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the importance of achieving emotional needs in character formation. ● Learners brainstorm on what emotional needs are and mention them in class (sad, happy, angry, fear, surprise, joy). ● Learners with low vision are guided to use digital devices with assistive technology to watch video clips or observe pictures of people expressing various emotions (sad, happy, angry, fear, surprise, joy) while learners with blindness listen to audio clips or picture descriptions of how people express the emotions (sad, happy, angry, fear, surprise, joy). ● In groups, learners are guided to simulate different ways of expressing emotions such as sadness, happiness, anger, fear, surprise and joy. ● Learners are guided to use digital devices with assistive technology to search for various emojis that show different emotions. ● Learners with low vision are guided to match pictures or emojis with the particular emotions. Learners with blindness to be given clear verbal descriptions of the pictures or emojis and guided to match them with emotions. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Family Needs (Emotional needs) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Love: learners portray a caring attitude when comforting others who are hurting.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: learner identifies different emotions expressed by self and others.

Link to other Learning Areas:

● Emotional needs can be used by learners when learning about God’s Creation in Religious Activities.

● The words used to express emotions relates with learning new words in Language Activities.
